reports.summary:
The core approach is small and idiomatic. It walks and observes each shadow root between a target and the root, and most of the spec works in jest probes: siblings at every nesting level, the hosts on the path, content and new shadow roots added later, live announcers and top-layer elements, targets in sibling shadow roots, revert, and flag-off behaviour. Overlays tests (193) and the type check pass.

Two problems block merging. First, the diff deletes the repo's custom ESLint rules (bin/imports.js, pure-render.js, useLayoutEffectRule.js), so `yarn eslint` crashes with ENOENT on './bin'. Second, when a target sits in a shadow root nested inside another target, content inside the outer target gets aria-hidden, which my probe reproduces.

Also, a shadow root that renders a slotted light-DOM target is never walked, so the web component's own shadow content stays exposed. The tests are good and follow the repo's style. The extra deletions alone would stop a maintainer from merging this as is.

They covered: targets in two separate shadow roots (input plus popover), with siblings hidden and later additions hidden; a slotted light-DOM target; a target nested in a shadow root inside another target, where nothing inside it is hidden; a new shadow host added to an enclosing root after the call, which is hidden; live-announcer and top-layer elements added at shadow depth, which stay visible; nested and out-of-order calls, with a full before/after snapshot restored exactly; inert mode; and undo stopping observation. The implementation is compact. It adds a slot-aware `flatContains`, walks the shadow root of any host that contains a target, records those roots, and observes them on the same MutationObserver. Everything is gated by `shadowDOM()`. The defects are all minor: closed shadow roots are silently ignored, `flatContains` partly duplicates the shared `nodeContains` helper, re-walking on resume happens for shadow roots but not for the light DOM, and the tests use a fixture-root workaround for observers leaked by earlier tests. A maintainer would likely merge this with small edits.
